swap.evidence: Products swapped in: a seed library and a village-hall room/equipment booking. Survive unchanged: masthead (icon + name in bold body type), sage ground, white bordered cards, single green accent, the repeated icon tile (swap the glyph), summary-list confirm, error summary, session radio cards. Bound to Fernhill: only copy — tool names and specs, deposits, Wed/Sat session times, '14 Mill Lane', 'run by volunteers'. With the name and copy hidden, a reader could tell it is a booking form but not that it lends tools.

Predicted opposite: a warm 'folksy' hand-drawn noticeboard look. The design matches the default on ground, accent, type, cards, error summary (confirm/errors/375-light) and summary lists (done/default/1280-light).

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online booking for a parish council's hall and folding-table loan, run by volunteers, mostly on phones'. Overlap is near total; nothing here was driven specifically by a tool library (no tools shown, no workshop/shed/card material).

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Detectors reported zero hits, so nothing anchored or changed; the verdicts stand. A tell-free detector result is consistent with a clean but generic page: absence of tells is not evidence of specificity.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench tile instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on find use an identical wrench glyph in a pale-green square as the thumbnail. The thumbnail occupies about a fifth of each card and distinguishes nothing; it reads as a placeholder left in place.
findings.impact: Members recognise tools by sight ('the drill with two batteries'); a picture of the actual item is likely to speed choice and gives the page its only possible content-led visual interest. Repeated identical tiles make the page look unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail is for: real photographs of the library's own items supplied by volunteers, or remove the tile and let the name lead. Do not keep a slot that shows nothing.

findings.title: Tool names truncated at 375 so the two drills look identical
findings.description: At 375 tool names are cut with an ellipsis: both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…', and 'Extension ladder 3 m …', 'Pressure washer, 130 …' lose the spec that distinguishes them.
findings.impact: Phones are the main device; members may open the wrong drill or need to open each to tell them apart. The distinguishing detail is exactly what the brief says members use ('two batteries').
findings.recommendation: Let names wrap on narrow widths, or reallocate the thumbnail's width to the name.

findings.title: Search and filters fall below the full tool list at 375
findings.description: On find at 375, 'Search tools', the Search button and the filter toggle appear after all ten cards, just above Opening times; at 768 and up they sit above the list.
findings.impact: The page's job is finding a tool; on phones the search is likely to be missed or reached only after a long scroll, and the layout order differs from wider widths.
findings.recommendation: Keep the search in the same position relative to the list at every width.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar cuts across the calendar and sits outside the content edge
findings.description: In the first viewport of the tool page the white action bar crosses the calendar (1280: through the first week row, clipping 'Open' under Sat 10; 375: over the Pick-up day help text). Its button ends at x≈1264 while all content ends at 1184.
findings.impact: The calendar is the step members must complete; a bar sliced through it at first view looks broken and may hide session marks. The misaligned button breaks the page's column.

factor_notes.persistence: Scrolling behaviour and bottom clearance are not assessable from stills.

findings.recommendation: Decide the bar's relation to the content column and ensure the calendar can be read in full above it.

findings.title: Details list uses two different label column widths
findings.description: On the tool page the Details list has Category/Deposit/Available from values at x≈224 and Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values at x≈180, with an extra gap between the two groups.
findings.impact: Reads as two lists pasted together; small but visible lapse against 'careful'.
findings.recommendation: Use one label column for the whole Details list, or separate the two groups with a heading.

findings.title: Basket sessions: orphan full-width row above five squeezed columns
findings.description: At 1280 the first session (Wed 28 Oct) spans full width while the other five sit in one row of narrow cards with three-line wraps ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00'). Sessions are also listed newest first.
findings.impact: The odd grid implies the first session is special and makes dates hard to scan; reverse order runs against how people read a calendar.
findings.recommendation: Choose a session layout that keeps every option the same shape at each width, in date order.

findings.title: Dark theme inverts availability chip emphasis
findings.description: In dark mode the 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' chips show green text with almost no visible fill, while later-availability chips ('Sat 17 Oct', 'Wed 21 Oct') keep a visible grey fill.
findings.impact: Most members use dark mode on phones; the not-yet-available tools look more prominent than the available ones, the reverse of the light theme.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark chip roles so available stays the emphasised state.

findings.title: Filter panel uses an unstyled native date input in yyyy/mm/dd
findings.description: 'Available from' is a browser-default date field showing 'yyyy/mm/dd', and its label sits higher than the Category label beside it.
findings.impact: The format contradicts the product's en-GB dates (Saturday 17 October) used everywhere else and the misaligned pair looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the date filter presents dates consistently with the rest of the product, and align the filter controls.

findings.title: No-results state shows the full list and no message
findings.description: The no-results capture has 'sewing machine' in the search field but shows all ten tools with no empty-state message.
findings.impact: Members may believe the listed tools match their search; no designed empty state exists to point them to the desk or other categories.

factor_notes.persistence: May be a capture that did not submit the search; verifier should check.

findings.recommendation: Design the empty state for a search with no matches.

findings.title: Wide layouts on confirm and done leave the right half empty
findings.description: At 1280 the summary boxes span the full 1088px frame but the form fields, note and 'What happens next' box stop at ~610px, leaving a large empty area on the right.
findings.impact: Mixed widths on one page look unplanned on desktop (lunch-break use); a sign of unfinish.
findings.recommendation: Choose one content width per page, or give the wide column a job.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name in bold body text
findings.description: The masthead is a small stroke wrench beside 'Fernhill Tool Library' in the body face; no screen carries anything of the library's world (the card, the desk, the shelves, the community centre).
findings.impact: 'Neighbourly' is carried by copy alone; the service is indistinguishable from any council booking form, which the brief's attributes do not ask for.
findings.recommendation: Decide one identity element drawn from the library's own world that can sit on every Operate surface without becoming a hero moment.

findings.title: Navigation items wrap to two lines at 375
findings.description: At 375 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)', 'Opening / times' each break across two lines under the name.
findings.impact: Ragged nav on the primary device; the basket count is split from its label.
findings.recommendation: Prevent nav labels from breaking at narrow widths.

findings.title: Membership number example breaks across lines in error text
findings.description: At 375 the inline error 'Enter your membership number, like FT-01234' breaks after 'FT-'.
findings.impact: Splits the exact format members must type, in the moment they are correcting it.

strengths: Copy is concrete and in the volunteers' voice: deposits, sessions, what to bring, 'Nothing is paid online'.
One filled primary per page and a clear H1 give an easy reading order.
Error summary plus inline errors on confirm are complete and well placed.
keep: Keep the plain, concrete volunteer voice and the one-primary-action discipline while adding identity.
